Organizational practice within the context of atrial fibrillation care encompasses the structural and operational models used to deliver patient treatment and education. A prominent example of this is the multidisciplinary approach adopted by specialized hospital units. Since the establishment of the [[atrieflimren-klinik|Atrieflimren-klinik]] in 2012, [[hospitalsenhed-midt|Hospitalsenhed Midt]] has maintained a continuous organizational focus on the education of patients and their relatives [^src1]. This reflects a broader practice of integrating patient empowerment and family involvement directly into the clinical workflow.

Furthermore, organizational practice extends beyond hospital walls to include the integration of external specialists into public healthcare pathways. For instance, [[praktiserende-kardiologer|Praktiserende kardiologer]] play a measurable role in the broader care system, with 15 practicing cardiologists involved in 5% of incident patient pathways [^src2]. This highlights a collaborative organizational model where specialized outpatient resources are leveraged to manage patient volume and ensure comprehensive care across different healthcare settings.
